directSourceFindings: workflow-engine.js validates Stage 24 acceptance and exact current productId, productVersion, and baselineId before FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE can create the Stage 25 candidate set.

The delivery candidate stores exact artifact identities, authorized filenames, byte lengths/hashes, package membership, and product lineage under application ownership; missing verified member bytes fail freeze.
validatedRepresentationInspections(project) selects only current accepted representation evidence bound to the exact current deliveryCandidateSetId, productId, productVersion, and baselineId.

deliveryCandidateSetMatches(project) requires the accepted representation inspection to cover exactly the candidate member artifact identities and rejects stale or mismatched product lineage, member bytes, filenames, and package membership.
Stage 25 gate evaluation remains false when no current accepted representation inspection exists and becomes true only for an exact current inspection of the frozen candidate set.

verify-delivery-candidate-representation.mjs invokes the actual engine functions against isolated invalid and repaired fixtures rather than accepting proof-file or source-string assertions as the oracle.

verification/verify-browser.mjs exercises the visible candidate/representation path under local Chromium, and the current main workflow also completed exact deployment-byte and deployed Chromium verification after the Stage 26 implementation merge.
repairedStateProofs: After Stage 24 is accepted and every candidate member has the required verified identity, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE creates the exact current immutable candidate set.

After a current accepted representation inspection is bound to the same candidate/product/version/baseline and exactly the candidate member artifact identities, the Stage 25 gate accepts the representation state.
The same engine match path that rejects changed member identity accepts the unchanged exact candidate and inspection, proving fail-before/progress-after behavior.
